en: The Ritual for Receiving the Bodhisattva Precepts, composed by the Śramaṇa Shi Huisi of Nanyue.
Regarding the Dharma for receiving the Mahāyāna precepts: first, one is instructed to request a single Bodhisattva precept-transmitting master to serve as the guide. First...
The petition is as follows. [The candidate] subsequently recites: "I, [Name], and others, now seek to receive the Bodhisattva precepts from the Venerable One.

May the Venerable One, out of compassion and without wearying yourself, grant them to me. This is said three times. The Precept Master then explains various causes, conditions, and skillful means, saying:
"Those who wish to seek the Dharma of the precepts must first give rise to faith. Once faith is established, the three trainings will be fully perfected."
The fruition of Buddhahood—the three bodies and four wisdoms—is certainly attainable; there should be no further doubt or anxiety. Thus, the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* states:

"Faith is the source of the Way and the mother of merit; it nurtures all roots of goodness, cuts through the net of doubt, and delivers one from the river of craving, revealing the unsurpassed path to Nirvāṇa.
Therefore, one should know that if the gate of faith is opened, one will necessarily receive the precepts. As for the precepts...
It is the vanguard of the myriad practices and the foundation of the six perfections. It is like constructing a palace:

if one first secures its foundation, yet merely builds upon empty space, it will certainly not be completed. Thus, the precepts are the provisions for the Great Way; the precepts are the raft for crossing the sea of suffering.
To adorn the Dharma-body, one takes the precepts as a necklace; to destroy afflictions, one takes the precepts as a source of coolness.

However, there are many varieties. By taking the three refuges and the five precepts, one obtains a human body. Through the ten wholesome actions and the eightfold fast, one receives the retribution of rebirth in the heavens.
By observing the ten precepts and the full set of monastic precepts, one crosses the river of afflictions and craving to attain the noble fruit of an Arhat.
Those who receive the Bodhisattva precepts shall attain the fruit of Buddhahood. The *Brahmajāla Sūtra* says: "All those with a mind should embrace the Buddha-precepts. [The assembly...]
Upon receiving the Buddha’s precepts, one attains entry into the rank of all Buddhas. Thus we know that all who possess a mind are fully endowed with the Buddha-precepts;
each is complete and without deficiency. Question: If this is so, why is it necessary to receive them again? Answer: Because they have been temporarily lost, the matter is clarified once more.
From this, one knows that the entire mind is the precepts, and the entire precepts are the mind. Apart from the mind, there are no precepts. Apart from...
The precepts have no mind. It is further said: "Listen, O Sons of the Buddha! Those who wish to receive the Buddha-precepts include kings, princes, ministers, and high officials;
bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs; the eighteen Brahmā heavens and the six heavens of the desire realm; commoners, eunuchs, lecherous men, and lecherous women."

Slaves, the eight classes of spirits, *vajra*-deities, animals, and even transformed beings—provided they understand the words of the Dharma Master, all may receive the precepts and are called the foremost pure ones.

Because their merit from the virtue of the precepts is immeasurable and their achievement surpasses that of the ten thousand phenomena, they serve as models for the five vehicles and as a vessel for the Three Jewels. The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* states: "Great evil..."
In sickness, the precepts are a potent medicine. Amidst great terror, the precepts are a protector. In the midst of profound darkness, the precepts are a bright lamp.
Amidst all perilous paths, the precepts are a bridge. In the waters of the great ocean, the precepts are a boat. The *Satyaka-sūtra* says:
"If one does not uphold the precepts, one cannot even attain the body of a jackal, let alone a body of merit. [End of] Moon [Chapter].
The *Dīpa-samādhi Sūtra* states: "Though one possesses noble lineage and great learning, if one lacks precepts and wisdom, one is like a bird or beast.

Though one dwells in a lowly station and has little learning, if one can maintain pure precepts, one is called a superior person. The single word for "precept" (*śīla*) is translated as "cooling," for it extinguishes the three karmas.
In Sanskrit, it is called *śīla*, or also *vinaya* and *prātimokṣa*. In Chinese, it is rendered as "cooling. It extinguishes the three types of karma.

From these transgressions, one attains liberation. Now, as for what is called "precept" (*śīla*): it can prevent the three evil realms and can cease the three delusions; thus, it receives its name from its very essence. As for this essence:

when one first gives rise to the perfect mind (*pariniṣpanna-citta*) and requests and receives the precepts from a teacher, the state of uplifted sincerity within the body is termed the "precept of action" (*kriyā-śīla*).

Its essence consists of matter and mind (*rūpa-citta*). Once the three *karmavācanā* (formal acts) are completed, the dharma is received and dwells within the breast; the essence of action then passes away.
The future is called the unconditioned precept (*asaṃskṛta-śīla*). It takes the mind of ultimate reality (*dharmatā-citta*) alone as its essence. Thus, the *Ratnavyuha Sūtra* states:
"The precepts of all noble ones and ordinary beings alike take the mind as their essence. Because the mind is inexhaustible, the precepts are also inexhaustible.

One should know that the object and the mind are in accord, and the subject and the object are mysteriously one. Since you, sons of the Buddha, each possess a heart of longing and yearning, [you should cultivate this].
One should listen to and receive this with earnest diligence and a focused mind.
There are eight kinds of excellence in the Bodhisattva precepts. What are these eight?
First is the excellence of the ultimate path: upon receiving the Bodhisattva precepts, one is like the great garuḍa bird, which, with a single beat of its wings, soars high and can travel ten...
It is over nineteen thousand *li*. This is because the path of the Bodhisattva precepts is swift; by generating the mind [of enlightenment], one transcends the six realms of existence.

Because it proceeds directly to unsurpassed *bodhi*, the second generation of the mind is superior. By generating in a single thought the mind of great compassion and wisdom, one surpasses the realm of the two vehicles (*śrāvaka* and *pratyekabuddha*).
It is like the story of two novices in the past who generated the *bodhicitta*; an *arhat* was reborn [as one of them].
1. Superiority in respect: [The bodhisattva] carries robes and bundles, yields the road, and so forth. 2. Superiority in the field of merit:
Even if one were to make offerings to as many arhats as would fill the entire Jambudvīpa, it would not equal the merit of a single great garuḍa bird;

for this bird has previously received the bodhisattva precepts. 4. Superiority in merit: Receiving the bodhisattva precepts is like the light of the sun, which shines everywhere. Receiving the śrāvaka [precepts]... [is not so].
The precepts are like the light of a firefly; their radiance is so faint that they cannot be compared [to the light of the sun]. Thus, the fivefold undertaking of the minor offenses is superior.
After one has received the Bodhisattva precepts, even if one should break them, it is still superior to being an outsider who has not received the precepts at all.

Outsiders hold false views and will sink forever into the evil realms with no prospect of escape; whereas a person who has broken the precepts, by virtue of the power of the precepts, even if they fall...
In the evil realms, their retribution for offenses will be slight. If they fall into hell, they will become kings within the hells; if they fall among animals, they will become kings of animals;
if they fall among ghosts, they will become kings of ghosts; if they are born among humans, they will become kings of men;

if they are born among devas, they will become kings of devas. In every place of rebirth, they shall not lose their royal status. Therefore, the Sūtra says: "There are those who commit transgressions..."

They are called Bodhisattvas. They possess precepts that can be broken; those who have no transgressions are called outsiders (*tīrthika*), because they have no precepts to break. Sixth, their dwelling in the womb is superior:
when a Bodhisattva dwells in the womb, he is constantly protected by the gods, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, and all the various benevolent divine kings.
Seventh, their supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) are superior: they can transform the great earth into gold and the seven treasures, and churn the long rivers into clarified butter and curd.
First, the excellence of the essence: because it can, in a single thought-moment, transcend hundreds of thousands of worlds and transform hundreds of thousands of sentient beings in a single day.

Second, the excellence of the retribution: because one is born into the Lotus Treasury Ocean, realizes the Dharma-nature body, and once having attained the true and eternal, never again undergoes regression.
Next, regarding the first of the five dharmas for those who wish to receive the bodhisattva precepts: First, one contemplates all sentient beings of the ten directions as being like noble sages.
Second, one contemplates all sentient beings of the ten directions as being like one’s own parents. Third, one contemplates all [sentient beings of the ten directions...]
One views all sentient beings as one would view a teacher. Fourth, one views all sentient beings in the ten directions as one would view a king.
Fifth, one views all sentient beings in the ten directions as one would serve a great lord.
Next, one should give rise to three vows:
first, the vow that the merit produced by the three karmas of oneself be shared in common with all sentient beings of the ten directions;
second, the vow that one, together with all sentient beings of the ten directions, may quickly cross the great ocean of birth-and-death and afflictions to reach nirvana.
The Other Shore. Third, may I and all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm thoroughly penetrate the words and meanings of the twelve divisions of the scriptures with complete clarity;
may all wholesome dharmas increase through the precepts, and may we be fully endowed with the six pāramitās and the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment.
Because they have attained profound meditative concentration, aroused the six supernormal powers, emitted great radiance, attained the knowledge of all modes, perfected the five eyes,
and accomplished the path of the Buddha.
Next, make the Four Great Vows (the Precept Master recites them three times):
Sentient beings are boundless; I vow to deliver them all. Afflictions are immeasurable; I vow to sever them all. Dharma gates are boundless;
I vow to study them all. The Buddha-way is unsurpassed; I vow to accomplish it.
Next, the invitation to the Precept Master is made as follows: "I, [Name], and others, now receiving the Bodhisattva precepts,
respectfully invite Śākyamuni Buddha to serve as our Upādhyāya (Preceptor),
and respectfully invite Mañjuśrī Nāga-jāti-agra-rāja Buddha to serve as our Karmācārya (Ritual Master)."
I respectfully invite the future Buddha Maitreya to serve as the *ācārya* who provides instruction;
I respectfully invite all the Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions to serve as the masters who witness the precepts.
I respectfully invite all the Great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions to act as my fellow students and companions (recite this three times).
If I should fall into the three evil realms and undergo great suffering and affliction, I pray that the Upādhyāya, the Ācārya, the Honored One,
the witnesses, the teachers, and my fellow students and companions will, out of compassion, rescue and deliver me, enabling me to attain liberation (recite this once).
With single-minded devotion, we entreat all Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time— whose true and responsive bodies pervade the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm—
as well as the twelve divisions of the scriptures, the ocean-treasury of True Suchness, and all great Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas:
may you all descend universally upon this site of practice to bear witness to and receive the merit of our precept-taking.
With single-minded devotion, we invoke the protectors of the Dharma and the precepts— the kings of the twenty-eight heavens throughout the ten directions and the dharma-realm,

including Śakra and Brahmā— as well as the eight classes of dragon deities. We pray that, by the power of the Triple Gem, you will all descend in unison upon this site of practice to purify and protect the precepts, and bear witness to our meritorious virtues.
With single-minded devotion, we invoke the Ten-Direction Dharma-realm beings of the six destinies and four modes of birth:

the Son of Heaven Yama, the Lord of Mount Tai, the officials of the Celestial and Earthly Courts, the deities of Life-Span and Emolument, the youths of Merit and Demerit, the dark officials of good and evil, the Generals of the Five Paths, and the Messengers who inflict disease.
We pray that all, by the power of the Triple Gem, will descend universally upon this site of practice, equally partake in the precepts and wholesome deeds, and bear witness.

Virtue. With single-minded devotion, we invite all deities—those of the Five Peaks and Four Rivers within the borders of [Name] Prefecture, as well as those of the netherworld and the visible world, of water and land, of city walls and local shrines—to this assembly.
We pray that, by the power of the Triple Gem, you will descend universally upon this site of practice, partake together in these precepts and virtues, and bear witness.

With merit and single-minded devotion, I respectfully invite all sentient beings of the twelve categories throughout the ten directions and the Dharma-realm; all conscious beings present in this assembly;

all deceased relatives who have received the precepts, whether long or recently passed; all household deities of the nine grades; and all lingering spirits, resentful ghosts, and souls whose karmic debts remain unresolved.

As for those who have attained liberation: may they all, by virtue of the power of the Triple Gem, reach the site of enlightenment and together partake in the merit of the precepts, with their virtues being witnessed and certified.
Having finished the invocations above, one should now pay respectful homage to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Upādhyāya Śākyamuni Buddha.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to Mañjuśrī Nāga-jāti-agrabhūta-rāja Buddha.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Honored Maitreya Buddha who will descend to be born in the future.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to all Buddhas throughout the limits of the past.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to all Buddhas throughout the limits of the future.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to all Buddhas throughout the limits of the present.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the great Bodhisattvas, my fellow students and companions, throughout the ten directions.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to all the Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the entire Sangha Jewel of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
Having completed the prostrations to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, each kneels upon the right knee and receives the Three Refuges (following the preceptor’s words in a loud voice).
[The preceptor] meets [the disciples] at such-and-such a place, and each addresses them by name:
"Disciples, so-and-so and the rest, from this life until the end of the future, we vow to take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, and take refuge in the Saṃgha."

I take refuge in the Buddha, the Honored One among two-legged beings. I take refuge in the Dharma, the Honored One free from desire. I take refuge in the Saṃgha, the Honored One among assemblies. (Recite this three times.
Disciple [Name], from this day forward, I have completed taking refuge in the Buddha; I have completed taking refuge in the Dharma; I have completed taking refuge in the Saṃgha. (Recite this once.
From this day forward, I shall honor the Buddha as my Teacher and shall no longer take refuge in demons, heretics, or external paths. May it be so.
May the Three Jewels compassionately embrace me. Out of their loving-kindness and pity—(recite this three times).
Next, ask the difficult question:
"O Son of the Buddha, from this day forward, are you able to abandon all evil associates? (Answer: "I am able. Hereafter, proceed according to this.)
"O Son of the Buddha, from this day forward, will you be able to constantly mindfully recollect the Buddha and draw near to spiritual friends?
O Son of the Buddha, from this day forward, even at the cost of your life, will you be able to refrain from violating the precepts?"
"O Son of the Buddha, from this day forward, will you be able to read and recite the Mahāyāna sūtras and inquire about their profound meanings?
O Son of the Buddha, from this day forward, if you see any sentient beings suffering in affliction, will you be able to rescue and protect them according to your strength?"
"O Son of the Buddha, from this day forward, are you able to give rise to deep faith in unsurpassed enlightenment?
O Son of the Buddha, from this day forward, are you able to provide offerings to the Triple Gem according to your capacity for as long as you live?"
"O Son of the Buddha, from this day forward, will you be able to abandon all indolence, arouse diligence, and zealously seek the path of the Buddha?
O Son of the Buddha, from this day forward, will you be able to renounce all that is difficult to renounce?"
"O Son of the Buddha, from this day forward, when afflictions arise regarding the five sensory objects, are you able to subdue the mind?
(Having asked thus.)
I reverently address all Buddhas of the ten directions and the assembly of Bodhisattvas throughout the great earth.
These sons and daughters of the Buddha, [name], seek to receive the Bodhisattva precepts from the assembly of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Sangha.

These sons and daughters of the Buddha have already developed true and profound faith and have established the seed of Bodhi. Out of the Buddhas’ compassion, may they grant them the Bodhisattva precepts.
The Bodhisattva Precepts (recited three times).
With all the Noble Ones as my teachers, having completed the witness and verification, may the Buddhas of the ten directions, with their supernatural powers and divine eye, all behold me.
It is as if it were before one's very eyes. Now, the precepts are the dharma of purity; only when the vessel of the body is pure can one be worthy of receiving them.
First, one must perform repentance to wash and cleanse the body and mind, just as one must launder old clothes before they can be dyed. Yet, since the Tathāgata has manifested his parinirvāṇa...

More than two thousand years have passed since then; the True Dharma has sunk into obscurity, and perverse winds have fanned out widely. Sentient beings, possessing meager merit, were born to encounter such a time;
even if they hear the teachings, none are able to believe and accept them. This is truly because their afflictions and attachments are heavy and their adherence to views is stubborn.

If one does not reform the past and cultivate the future, there is no way for transgressions to be extinguished. If transgressions are not extinguished, the categories of precepts will not arise. If the categories of precepts do not...
The aspiration has been made, yet liberation remains difficult to expect. I now request the Buddhas of the ten directions and the great Bodhisattvas to act as witnesses.
By the great vows of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, may all sentient beings become no different from the Buddhas themselves.

We, the disciples [Name], from the day of the [month] of the [year], at such-and-such monastery in such-and-such village of such-and-such country on Jambudvīpa in the south, have received the Bodhisattva precepts.
(One should instruct them in the confession of the three karmas, saying:)
We, [Name] and others, from beginningless time until this day, have committed many unwholesome deeds of body—killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct;
unwholesome deeds of speech—lying, frivolous talk, slander, and harsh words; and unwholesome deeds of mind—covetousness, anger, and wrong views.
Through these three types of karma, we have committed immeasurable and boundless transgressions, both by our own actions and by inciting others to do so. Today, we feel shame...

I feel shame. I confess and repent openly. May my transgressions be extinguished and merit arise. May I behold the Buddha and hear the Dharma, and resolve to attain Bodhicitta (recite this three times).
He further says: "You have finished your confession; your three karmas are purified like lapis lazuli, pure both within and without, and thus worthy to receive the Bodhisattva precepts.
Only after questioning you regarding the prohibitions and obstacles shall you receive the pure precepts. Therefore, the Sūtra says: "If there are the seven prohibitions... [present...]
"One may not receive the precepts [if these conditions exist]. Now I ask you; answer each question truthfully as it is.
Son of the Buddha, have you ever shed the blood of a Buddha? (Answer: No. Hereafter, answer accordingly.
Have you ever killed your father? Have you ever killed your mother? Have you ever killed your *upādhyāya*? Have you ever killed your *ācārya*?"
Have you ever disrupted a *karmavācanā* or a *dharmacakra-pravartana* assembly? Have you ever killed a noble person (*ārya*)?

If you can answer "no" to all these questions, you are fit to receive the precepts. (I request the lay disciples—whether male or female—to rise and don the *kāṣāya*. There is great cause and effect [in this]; I shall not elaborate further here, but will explain it as the occasion arises.)
"O sons of the Buddha, you must arouse a mind of single-minded concentration and a heart of earnest devotion. Now I wish to bestow the precepts upon you.
If your minds are focused and determined, like an upright vessel turned upward, you will surely achieve success. If for even a single thought you deviate, it will be like an inverted vessel;
in the end, nothing can be contained within it. These precepts have no form or color, yet they can flow into your bodies and minds, lasting until the end of the future."
One will achieve the great fruit; yet at that time, there shall be no conscious perception.

If any form or color enters your body, it shall produce a sound like the collapsing of heavens and the cracking of the earth. You must maintain mindfulness and must not entertain other perceptions or any other thoughts.
(Since the arousal of the precepts is conditioned by such awareness.)
Next, regarding the formal reception of the precepts, first the three characteristics are briefly indicated. The three characteristics are: first, the precept of restraining oneself from misconduct;

second, the precept of gathering virtuous dharmas; and third, the precept of benefiting sentient beings. (Next, the presiding officiant shall perform the *jñapti-tri-karman* [the motion and three proclamations] and should say:

"Now, for the purpose of performing the threefold proclamation of the *karman*, you should give rise to the most supreme resolve (*uttamottama-citta*) and seek to receive the most supreme grade of precepts. Upa...
Regarding those who uphold the precepts: having received these precepts, they proceed toward Buddhahood with single-minded devotion; this is called the "highest-of-the-high" grade of mind.

You all should now listen attentively. At the time of the first *karmavācanā* (formal ritual motion), the subtle and wondrous dharma of the precepts throughout all realms in the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm will all vibrate and shift, and before long, they shall enter into your very bodies.
Sons of the Buddha, listen attentively. You now seek to receive from me the Bodhisattva precepts, namely:

the precept of restraining one’s conduct, the precept of gathering virtuous dharmas, and the precept of benefiting sentient beings. Sons of the Buddha, these precepts are the path traversed by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
The Buddhas of the past have already taught them; the Buddhas of the future shall teach them; and the Buddhas of the present are teaching them now. Past...
It is that which all bodhisattvas of the past have already received, studied, understood, practiced, and accomplished;
all bodhisattvas of the future will receive, study, understand, practice, and accomplish;
and all bodhisattvas of the present are now receiving, studying, understanding, practicing, and accomplishing—thereby destined to become Buddhas.
At the time of the second *karmavācanā*, this sublime dharma of the precepts arises above all phenomena within the *dharmadhātu* and pervades the entirety of space;
it gathers upon the crown of your head, and you should receive it with reverence.
"Sons of the Buddha, listen attentively (until): 'In the future you shall become Buddhas.
At the time of the third *karmavācanā*, this sublime dharma of the precepts enters into your body, becoming pure and complete.
It is precisely at this moment that you must receive the dharma of the precepts; you must not harbor other perceptions or thoughts that would cause the precepts to be incomplete."
"Sons of the Buddha, listen attentively... [until] you shall become Buddhas in the future.
Sons of the Buddha, the threefold *karmavācanā* is now completed; you are from this moment forth true Bodhisattvas, truly named sons of the Buddha."
Therefore, the *Mahākaruṇā-sūtra* states: "The initial resolve and the ultimate [attainment] are not two; of these two minds, the former is more difficult. The *Ratnakūṭa-śikhara-sūtra* states:
"The precept of restraint (*saṃvara-śīla*) refers to the ten grave precepts; the precept of the true Dharma (*saddharma-śīla*) refers to the eighty-four thousand dharma-gates;
and the precept of gathering sentient beings (*sattva-saṃgraha-śīla*) refers to the four means of integration (*catvāri saṃgrahavastūni*). All that you have asked thus far...
"I am able. "I shall now receive for you the ten inexhaustible precepts. You must listen with single-minded attention to each one.

O Son of the Buddha: from this present body until the attainment of the Buddha-body, throughout the entire future, in the interval between them, you must not intentionally take the life of any sentient being.
Should there be anyone who commits the act of killing, it is not the conduct of a Bodhisattva; they lose the forty-two stages of the Sages."
The Noble Dharma must not be transgressed. Can you uphold it? (He answers: "I can uphold it. Hereafter, proceed according to this.
O Son of the Buddha, from this present body until the attainment of the Buddha-body, throughout the limits of the future, during that interval, you must not commit theft.
If there is one who commits it, it is not the practice of a Bodhisattva; they lose the Dharma of the forty-two stages of the Sages and Worthies. It must not be transgressed.
"Can you uphold this?
O Son of the Buddha, from this present body until you attain the body of a Buddha, throughout the entire extent of the future, you must not engage in sexual desire during that interval.
Should you violate this, it is not the practice of a Bodhisattva; you will lose the dharmas of the forty-two stages of the worthy and holy ones. You must not violate it."
"Can you uphold this?
Son of the Buddha, from this present body until the attainment of the Buddha-body, throughout the entirety of the future limit, during that interval, you must not speak falsely.
Should you violate this, it is not the practice of a Bodhisattva; you will lose the dharmas of the forty-two stages of the worthy and holy ones. You must not violate it."
"Can you uphold this?
O Son of the Buddha, from this present body until the attainment of the Buddha-body, throughout the entire extent of the future, you must not sell alcohol during that interval.
Should you violate this, it is not the practice of a Bodhisattva; you will lose the dharma of the forty-two stages of the worthy and holy ones. You must not commit such an offense."
"Can you uphold this?

O Son of the Buddha, from this present body until the attainment of the Buddha-body, throughout the entire span of the future, you must not speak of the faults of bodhisattvas, whether they be householders or renunciants.
Should you violate this, it shall not be considered the conduct of a bodhisattva, and you will lose the forty-two [bodhisattva stages]."
These are the dharmas of the ranks of the noble ones; they must not be transgressed. Can you uphold them?
O Son of the Buddha, from this present body until the attainment of the Buddha-body, throughout the entirety of the future, during that interval, you must not harbor stinginess or greed.
If there should be a transgression, it is not the practice of a Bodhisattva; one loses the dharmas of the forty-two ranks of the noble ones. They must not be transgressed.
"Can you uphold this?
Son of the Buddha, from this present body until the attainment of the Buddha-body, throughout the entirety of the future, in the interval between them, you must not give way to anger.
Should you violate this, it would not be the conduct of a Bodhisattva; you would lose the dharmas of the forty-two stages of the worthy and holy ones. You must not violate it."
"Can you uphold this?

Son of the Buddha, from this present body until the attainment of the Buddha-body, throughout the entirety of the future, in the interval between them, you must not praise yourself while disparaging the faults of others.
Should you violate this, it is not the conduct of a Bodhisattva, and you shall lose the forty-two stages of the noble ones."
Dharma. You must not violate it. Can you uphold it?
O Son of the Buddha, from this present body until the attainment of Buddhahood, throughout the entire future, during that interval, you must not slander the Triple Gem.
If there should be one who violates this, it is not the practice of a Bodhisattva; they shall lose the Dharma of the forty-two stages of the worthy and holy ones. It is not...
"Can you maintain them?
Son of the Buddha, by maintaining these ten grave precepts as they are, you shall be fully endowed with the ten pāramitās and achieve the body of a Buddha."
Endowed with merit, you shall attain great supernormal powers and emit great radiance, and you shall attain all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Why is this? Because you uphold the precept against killing, you shall obtain an indestructible adamantine body (*vajrakāya*), and your lifespan shall be immeasurable kalpas, beyond exhaustion.
He upholds the precept against stealing and fulfills the dāna-pāramitā.

He manifests bodies throughout the worlds of the ten directions, appearing in the forms of Śakra, Brahmā, the Four Heavenly Kings, various minor kings, śramaṇas, and others, using the gift of wealth to deliver sentient beings.
By upholding the precept against sexual misconduct, one attains the mark of the horse’s concealed organ and a body of golden hue. When sentient beings see this, their fear is immediately dispelled;
they abandon desire and sever the afflictions. One’s fame becomes universally renowned, and all who hear it rejoice.

By upholding the precept against false speech, one attains the four kinds of unimpeded eloquence: unimpeded eloquence regarding phenomena (*dharma-pratisaṃvid*), unimpeded eloquence regarding meaning (*artha-pratisaṃvid*), unimpeded eloquence regarding language (*nirukti-pratisaṃvid*), and unimpeded eloquence regarding inspired speech (*pratibhāna-pratisaṃvid*).
When preaching with a single voice, all sentient beings who hear it attain liberation.

By observing the precept against selling alcohol, one attains great intelligence. Within a single thought-moment, one hears the speech of all Buddhas of the ten directions as well as the speech of all sentient beings;
one also knows the minds of all Buddhas and the minds of all sentient beings, and attains the Samādhi of the Assemblage of All Buddhas.

By upholding the precept of not speaking of the faults of lay or ordained bodhisattvas, one attains the exhaustion of outflows (*āsravakṣaya*), the five eyes, and the six supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), as well as the complete realization of the three knowledges (*vidyā*) and other such dharmas.

By upholding the precept of non-avarice and non-greed, one attains the all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvākārajñatā*) endowed with unimpeded mastery; and among sentient beings who behold such a person, there are none who do not [revere them].

He resolves his mind [on enlightenment] and maintains the precept of non-anger; he attains the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics, such that all sentient beings who see him resolve their minds on bodhicitta.
By upholding the precept of not praising oneself or disparaging others, one shall be joyfully praised by ordinary beings and sages throughout the ten directions in every place of rebirth;
those who hear your name shall all abide in the stage of non-retrogression.
By upholding the precept of not slandering the Triple Gem, one attains the complete and perfect holy path of the Three Vehicles. With a single voice, the Dharma is preached;

its sound fills the ten directions, causing all sentient beings to awaken to the Way simultaneously and all to attain Buddhahood. (Please have the Precept Master recite the following declaration on behalf of the recipient of the precepts.)
I reverently address all Buddhas throughout the entirety of the void realm of the ten directions.

Before this image of the Buddha at the monastery in such-and-such a village, such-and-such a district, such-and-such a county, and such-and-such a state within the Great Yuan Nation on Jambudvīpa in this world, there are many disciples who have come to me and requested to receive the Bodhisattva precepts. I pray that all Buddhas will act as witnesses for them.
A second time:

"O Sons of the Buddha, throughout the buddha-fields of the ten directions at this very moment, there appear various signs such as cool breezes, extraordinary fragrances, extraordinary sounds, and radiance.
When those bodhisattvas behold these extraordinary signs, they each ask their respective Buddhas: 'By what causes and conditions have these appeared?'"

Auspicious signs appeared. That Buddha told him: "In such-and-such a country, at such-and-such a place, there are many sons of the Buddha who have completed receiving the Bodhisattva precepts from a certain master.
They now request me to serve as their witness; therefore, these signs have appeared. All the Bodhisattvas then praised this in unison.
In this most evil world, to be able to give rise to such an unsurpassed mind is truly rare; it inspires deep compassion.
Therefore, you must protect it with a sincere heart. O sons of the Buddha, you have now completed receiving the Bodhisattva precepts.
One transcends the four māras and overcomes the suffering of the three realms. If one can receive and uphold this, practicing according to the teaching, such a person is a hero among gods and humans.
If you violate it and fail to uphold it, you are not a bodhisattva, nor are you a hero among gods and humans;
you are called a beast, one of wrong views, and a non-Buddhist. This precept is named "Inexhaustible"; it may only be received again and must never be abandoned. One vows to deliver all beings.
Sentient beings are inexhaustible; this precept is inexhaustible because the kalpas of expounding the Dharma cannot be exhausted. This precept is inexhaustible.
The *Yingluo jing* (Sutra of the Necklaces) states: "The bodhisattva precepts of all ordinary beings and sages take the mind as their essence.
Because the mind is inexhaustible, the precepts are also inexhaustible."
Next, one should offer prostrations of gratitude to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
With a sincere heart, pay reverent homage to the Upādhyāya Śākyamuni Buddha.
With a sincere heart, pay reverent homage to the Karmācārya Nāgottamarāja Buddha.
With a sincere heart, I pay respectful homage to the Preceptor Ācārya, the Honored Buddha Maitreya.
With a sincere heart, I pay respectful homage to the Honored Teachers who certify the precepts, the Buddhas of the ten directions.
With a sincere heart, I pay respectful homage to my fellow practitioners and companions, the Great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions.
Next, kneeling with the right knee on the ground and joining the palms, the *Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra* states:
"Those who receive the Bodhisattva precepts, although they have not yet attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, have already obtained these five kinds of meritorious qualities:

first, they are constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; second, in birth after birth and from lifetime to lifetime, they always experience supreme and wondrous happiness; third, when facing [death]..."
Fourth, after the end of life, one will be reborn in the worlds of all Buddhas.
Fifth, one will adorn *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"O sons and daughters of good family, I have now finished expounding the inexhaustible precepts for you all.
Having now completed the reception of the dharma of the inexhaustible precepts, you are true bodhisattvas who have resolved upon bodhicitta;

you are true children of the Buddha, born from the Buddha’s own mouth, born from the True Dharma, fully endowed with the practice of the precepts, correctly directed toward the path of the Buddha, having transcended the four māras, and having surpassed the three..."
To transcend the realms of suffering is true diligence, true valor, true dedication toward the Buddha-way, and true deliverance of sentient beings.

By the fruit and retribution of the merit from receiving these precepts, may one, in birth after birth and age after age, seek not the pleasures of minor regional kings, universal wheel-turning monarchs, Śakra, Brahmā, or the heavens of the three realms.
If one can thus receive and uphold [the precepts] and practice according to the teaching, [this is true dedication].
Practitioner, you are called a Bodhisattva, a celestial being, and a great man.

By means of these merits, dedicate them to all sentient beings throughout the ten directions of the Dharma-realm, so that they may together aspire to Bodhi and collectively attain the Buddha-way. If one breaks the precepts and does not uphold them, one is neither a Bodhisattva nor a celestial being or great man;
such a person is called a non-Buddhist (tīrthika) and shall fall into the three miserable realms and the eight difficult conditions. Nevertheless, I vow to receive [the teachings].

I exhort all you sons of the Buddha: may the spirits of nine generations of ancestors be reborn together in the Pure Land; may our six types of close relatives and loved ones all cause the sprouts of goodness to grow;
may all beings within the four modes of existence and the nine states of being realize the principle of True Suchness; and may those in the eight difficulties all ascend the gate of liberation.

May the eight classes of beings, dragons, devas, and the worthy sages filling the void, all attend this supreme assembly; and may those in the three miserable realms together form auspicious karmic bonds with all sentient beings possessing consciousness.
Together we shall perfect the Buddha-way.
O sons of the Buddha, after you have received these precepts, may this body of mine abide within the Dharma-realm;
and may all sentient beings who behold me, you, and the various bodhisattvas assembled here, all resolve to attain unexcelled Bodhicitta—even including the mountains and rivers.
The great earth, grasses, trees, and forests also give rise to this mind, with every thought-moment uninterrupted until the attainment of Buddhahood and ultimate perfection.
For those who have not yet given rise to this mind, they manifest terrifying forms to compel them to do so, ensuring that they ultimately ascend to the shore of enlightenment.
O Sons of the Buddha, after receiving these precepts, this body shall pervade the entire Dharma-realm until the end of the future.
Throughout the four modes of deportment, it shall constantly expound the Dharma-gate of the Mind-Ground.

Even when manifesting as bodies for animals, various species, trees, or mountain forests, it shall always perform this teaching without ceasing from moment to moment, shaking the palaces of Māra and subduing the heterodox, so as to—
May all sentient beings with false views abandon their various attachments and enter into right view.

May they attain the essential meaning as it should be expressed, universally causing all sentient beings to enter the realm of the perfect, eternal, and mind-only state, transmitting it to one another without interruption.

May the Three Jewels as a single essence eternally manifest in the world. Furthermore, may this body constantly propagate the Great Teaching, interpreting its meanings and explaining the sutras so as to accord with the Buddha’s mind and harmonize with the profound intent.
Should there be any speech regarding worldly conventions, may it all conform to the True Dharma; may all activities for livelihood and production enter the Perfect School.
May the great banner of the Dharma be erected and the life-force of the Buddha’s wisdom be sustained, such that a single lamp can transmit itself to a hundred others.

A thousand lamps, each lamp inexhaustible within the others, universally causing all who hear to suddenly realize their own minds, ascend the gate of ultimate liberation, and enter the ocean of numinous wisdom (*prajñā*).
Thereafter, for all sentient beings within the dharma-realm who invoke my name:
Those who behold my form shall all abide in their original station and never regress from the true and eternal. They shall manifest traces throughout the ten directions;
fire cannot burn them, water cannot drown them, medicine cannot affect them, poison cannot harm them, calamities cannot invade them, and enmity cannot ensnare them.
May all who are blind gain sight; may those who are deaf gain hearing; may those who are mute be able to speak; and may those who are lame be able to walk.
Thereafter, this body shall transform into infinite bodies that travel throughout the ten directions to attend upon and make offerings to all Buddhas.
Then, with these bodies, one shall enter the cauldrons of boiling water and the furnaces of glowing coals to undergo suffering on behalf of all sentient beings. Or, toward...

Shaking his mendicant’s staff at the gates of hell, he sometimes emitted light within the prisons. The sharp points of the sword-trees were blunted, and the blades on the mountain of knives fell away.

Each being repented of their past karma and fully awakened to the Buddha-vehicle. When the text of the precepts was concluded, he universally exhorted all the male disciples present in the assembly to together sincerely recite the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā*, wishing that they may obtain whatever they desire.
The Ritual for Receiving the Bodhisattva Precepts (End)
